title: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Subsidised health screening in Healthier SG
sections.summary: Healthier SG subsidises health screening to detect illness earlier while keeping the co-payment approach for a sustainable healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Subsidising health screening in Healthier SG so that illness can be detected earlier, treated upstream, reducing the burden of human suffering down the line years later, all this while maintaining the approach of co-payment established many years ago as part of keeping Singapore's healthcare system sustainable.

sections.label: Frequent outpatient visits before COVID-19
sections.summary: 2019 figures showed over 7,000 patients had 24 or more outpatient visits a year, and over 2,000 had 36 or more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The 2019 figures from before COVID-19 showed that over 7,000 patients had 24 or more outpatient visits a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In short, on average, two outpatient visits a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: There were over 2,000 patients with 36 or more outpatient visits a year, averaging three or more a month for an entire year.

sections.label: Reducing clinic trips helps caregivers
sections.summary: Reducing clinic trips and delivering care closer to home helps patients and caregivers, especially lower-wage workers with less workplace bargaining power.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have Clementi sons and daughters – filial, caring for their parents – but they had to give up their careers to accompany their parents for treatment, the many visits each month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, if we can reduce the number of trips to the clinic, have more care delivered closer to home, it will help patients and caregivers, especially workers who find it harder to take leave and take time-off; workers who are lower-wage; with less bargaining power at the workplace; workers with jobs that cannot be done remotely.

sections.label: MediFund mutual recognition agreements
sections.summary: Last November, Minister for Health Ong Ye Kung announced mutual recognition agreements for MediFund across hospitals and between acute and step-down care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last November, Minister for Health Ong Ye Kung, announced the roll-out of mutual recognition agreements for MediFund across hospitals and between acute hospitals and step-down care, intermediate care hospitals.

sections.label: Private hire fares for treatment
sections.summary: In one month, a family spent more than $400 on private hire vehicle fares to get their less mobile loved one to treatment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In one month, the family had clocked up more than $400 in private hire vehicle fares just to get their loved one to treatment because their loved one was less mobile.

sections.label: Clementi Polyclinic redevelopment announcement
sections.summary: In June 2022, MOH announced the Clementi Polyclinic would be redeveloped at a new site 650 metres away and 250 metres from Clementi MRT station.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In June 2022, MOH announced that the Clementi Polyclinic would be redeveloped at a new site, about 650 metres away from the existing site and 250 metres from the Clementi MRT station.

sections.label: Clementi MRT shelter request
sections.summary: An MP asks whether a shelter across Clementi Avenue 3 is feasible given the polyclinic's location within 400 metres of Clementi MRT.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And my Clementi residents have been keeping up to date on LTA policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: They have read LTA’s explanation of the Walk2Ride programme, and I quote, “Where feasible, walkways have been built to schools, healthcare facilities and other public amenities within a 400-metre radius of MRT stations.” The new polyclinic is a healthcare facility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The new polyclinic is within 400-metres from Clementi MRT.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, can I ask the Ministries, MOH and the Government more broadly, surely it would be feasible to build that shelter across Clementi Avenue 3 to help seniors and less mobile residents?

sections.label: Doctor-to-population ratio tracking
sections.summary: MOH is asked whether it tracks the doctor-to-population ratio and how Singapore compares with other advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH tell us, is it tracking the doctor-to-population ratio and how Singapore compares with other advanced economies, in particular, the doctor-to-population ratio when we look at public sector doctors serving the Singaporean population?

sections.label: Measuring actual clinical workload
sections.summary: The passage states that six five-minute consultations differ from a 30-minute consultation and that work done and needed must be measured accurately.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because six consultations of five minutes each are not the same as a 30-minute consultation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, we need to accurately measure how much work is actually being done on the ground, how much work is needed for tomorrow so that we can do right by our patients, caregivers and healthcare workers.

sections.label: Access and payment for new treatments
sections.summary: MOH is asked about equitable access to cell, tissue and gene therapy products and about new billing models such as no cure, no pay.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Is MOH working to ensure fair, equitable access to new treatments, such as cell, tissue and gene therapy products?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For certain new treatments where the chance of success is very slim, but the cost is very high, are there new billing models such as a “no cure, no pay” funding model?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Expensive drug, if it does not work, does not cure the patient, is there a refund from the manufacturer?

sections.label: Emergency department waiting times
sections.summary: MOH publishes daily median emergency department waiting times with a two-week delay, and median bed waits exceeded 16 hours at two hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOH currently publishes the daily median waiting time at emergency departments on a delayed basis of two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In some hospitals, even at the median, the waiting time for a bed can exceed 16 hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This was the situation at the end of January at Khoo Teck Puat and Changi General Hospital.

sections.label: Publishing ward admission percentiles
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to publish ward admission waiting times at the 75th and 90th percentiles, not just the median.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to have a more accurate perspective of the problem, would the Ministry be prepared to publish the waiting time for an admission to a ward, not just at the median which it does now, but at the 75th and 90th percentiles as well, for a more holistic overview of the situation on the ground?

sections.label: Increase in hospital beds
sections.summary: The Ministry announced plans to increase beds by 1,900 over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry has announced plans to increase beds over the next five years and the number is 1,900.

sections.label: Mobile Inpatient Care at Home pilot
sections.summary: The MIC@Home pilot admitted around 1,000 patients by June last year, saving an estimated 7,000 bed days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Mobile Inpatient Care at Home (MIC@Home) pilot seems to be demonstrating the potential of transforming patient care by providing a sustainable alternative to traditional hospital settings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I was encouraged to read from a Straits Times article in August 2023 that, as of June last year, around 1,000 patients have been admitted to the programme, staying for seven days on average, and resulting in an estimated savings of 7,000 bed days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: By end of 2023, more than 2,000 patients would have experienced the virtual wards according to the article.

sections.label: MediShield Life enhancements and expenditure
sections.summary: MediShield Life has been enhanced, and out-of-pocket expenditure fell from 48.1% in 2000 to 18.9% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MediShield Life has undergone several rounds of enhancement to ensure that Singaporeans can continue to afford paying for large hospital bills in times of catastrophic medical episodes and selected costly outpatient treatments, such as dialysis and chemotherapy for cancer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad to note from the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Health Expenditure database that the out-of-pocket expenditure in terms of percentage of the current health expenditure in Singapore has decreased between years 2000 and 2020 from 48.1% to 18.9%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is also note-worthy that eight in 10 Singaporeans pay little or no cash for their subsidised hospital bills.

sections.label: GP clinics and primary care
sections.summary: About 80% of primary care demand in Singapore is met by GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, in Singapore, about 80% of our primary care demand are met by our GP clinics.

sections.label: Healthier SG implementation progress update
sections.summary: The passage asks about Healthier SG progress, healthcare manpower retention, eight remaining polyclinics by 2030, and system integration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like ask the Ministry regarding the progress update for Healthier SG implementation thus far.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, whether the manpower, infrastructure and systems implementation plans are keeping pace with the timeline and envisioned capacity of the national healthcare system as it pivots to Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the Government announced last month regarding changes to and guidance on the salary of our nurses, but are there similar concerns and plans for the retention of other healthcare professionals including doctors and allied health professionals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also wonder whether the remaining eight polyclinics slated to be open by 2030 are on track, and whether there have been any challenges to the system integration efforts between private GPs, polyclinics and hospital clusters to realise the full potential of Healthier SG over time.

sections.label: Healthier SG chronic tier subsidies
sections.summary: The rollout of Healthier SG chronic tier subsidies and encouraging GPs to manage more chronic conditions is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The recent rollout of Healthier SG chronic tier subsidies and the broader direction to encourage GPs to manage more chronic conditions, is welcomed news.

sections.label: EASE 2.0 for seniors
sections.summary: HDB will roll out EASE 2.0 from 1 April, expanding the wireless Alert Alarm System to benefit more seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Similarly, improving our seniors’ home environment through initiatives like EASE 2.0 is important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am glad the Housing and Development Board (HDB) is going to roll-out EASE 2.0 from 1 April onwards, which includes the expansion of the wireless Alert Alarm System to benefit more seniors.

sections.label: Hospital wait times and capacity
sections.summary: Medium wait times at two hospitals can exceed half a day, and planned expansions may remain insufficient as the population grows and ages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Medium wait times at the end of January can still exceed half a day in Changi General and Khoo Teck Puat, while the bed occupancy rate for all but one of the public hospitals hovers above the Ministry's own preferred 80% ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, the planned expansion of Alexandra Hospital and the Woodlands Health Campus is likely to only fix current shortfalls, but remain insufficient as our population grows and ages.

sections.label: Ramping up urgent care
sections.summary: Urgent care offerings can be ramped up as an intermediate option complementing GP polyclinics versus A&E solutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, we can ramp up our urgent care offerings as an intermediate option, complementing existing GP polyclinics versus A&E solutions.

sections.label: Transition care and non-profit model
sections.summary: Incentives for transition care at home could be improved, and the non-profit model's viability hinges on tax exemptions and operational flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, we can improve the incentives for transition care at home, perhaps with cash incentives paid directly to patients using savings that would otherwise go toward hospitalisation expenses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, while I support the decision to expand the non-profit model, whether the experiment will ultimately prove viable, will also hinge crucially on whether the associated tax exemptions are accompanied by increased or decreased flexibility of operations.

sections.label: SCDF ambulances stuck at hospital
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about a report that 12 of 92 SCDF ambulances were stuck at Changi General Hospital on 29 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, I am deeply concerned about the recent report in The Straits Times regarding the predicament of 12 ambulances, out of a fleet of 92 Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) ambulances, being stuck at Changi General Hospital on 29 January 2024.

sections.label: Singapore hospital beds ratio
sections.summary: Singapore's ratio of hospital beds per 1,000 people stood at approximately 2.55 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore's ratio of hospital beds per 1,000 people stood at approximately 2.55 in 2023, last year.

sections.label: Medical school rejections and doctor ratio
sections.summary: About 2,400 Singaporeans are rejected yearly from NUS and NTU medical schools, and Singapore has 2.8 doctors per 1,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As a result, some have to go overseas to study medicine, imposing a significant financial burden on their parents and contributing to a brain drain from Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: We understand that about 2,400 Singaporeans applied to medical schools at the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU) every year but were rejected due to an intake of only about 510 students per cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore's doctor-to-population ratio stands at 2.8 doctors per 1,000 people, which is quite low compared to countries like the United Kingdom, 3.2; United States, 3.6; Australia, 4.1; and the EU average of 4.3 doctors per 1,000 people.

sections.label: HSA anti-vaping enforcement doubts
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister to give insights into HSA's enforcement team size and effectiveness and the vaping scene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: This raises doubts about the priority placed on anti-vaping efforts within HSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Minister to provide insights into the size and effectiveness of the HSA's enforcement team and whether the Minister is satisfied with the current state of the vaping scene in Singapore.

sections.label: Rising healthcare expenditure sustainability
sections.summary: Healthcare expenditure has skyrocketed over the past decade, raising questions about sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, healthcare expenditure has skyrocketed, raising questions about sustainability as well.

sections.label: Nurse retention and welfare initiatives
sections.summary: The nurse retention scheme and initiatives to improve healthcare workers' welfare are welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The recently unveiled nurse retention scheme as well as initiatives to improve healthcare workers' welfare are all welcomed.

sections.label: Buying medication without consultation
sections.summary: Cost concerns drive some Singaporeans to buy prescription medication online and over the counter across the border without medical consultation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Beyond medical procedures, cost concerns are driving some Singaporeans to buy prescription medication from online marketplaces and over the counter across the border without prior medical consultation, potentially jeopardising their healthcare.

sections.label: Day surgery versus inpatient costs
sections.summary: A surgical procedure done in a day surgery setting costs significantly less than the same procedure done as an inpatient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Costs of a surgical procedure done in a day surgery setting is significantly much lower than that of a same procedure done as inpatient of the hospital.

sections.label: A&E overuse and bed shortage
sections.summary: Proximity to hospitals contributes to overuse of A&E for non-emergencies, causing gridlock and bed shortage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Because of the small size of our island, proximity to hospitals is a blessing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But it is also contributing to the overuse of A&E services for non-emergencies, resulting in a gridlock at the A&E and also a knock-on effect on bed shortage.

sections.label: SMA patients and Risdiplam
sections.summary: Without treatment, SMA patients face deterioration and respiratory failure, while HSA-approved Risdiplam improves motor function and stabilises progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Without treatment, SMA patients like Sherry face the grim prospect of progressive deterioration, respiratory failure and a bedridden future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is an HSA-approved oral medication called Risdiplam, which improves motor function and stabilises SMA's progression.

sections.label: Risdiplam annual cost
sections.summary: An annual supply of Risdiplam costs $375,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An annual supply of Risdiplam costs $375,000 per year.

sections.label: Urging MOH to expedite review
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to expedite its review of SMA treatments for subsidies and mainstream financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Every day without treatment access is a missed opportunity to improve their quality of life and prolong lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge MOH to expedite its review of SMA treatments for subsidies and mainstream financing.

sections.label: Sherry's medication fundraising shortfall
sections.summary: She has reached only 12% of her $375,000 target for one year's supply of medication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, she has only managed to reach 12% of her $375,000 target, just to secure one year's supply of medication.

sections.label: Cancer diagnoses and deaths
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2021, an average of 46 people per day were diagnosed with cancer and 16 died of it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Cancer Society, over the five-year period from 2017 to 2021, an average of 46 people per day were diagnosed with cancer in Singapore, while 16 people per day died of it.

sections.label: Elective egg freezing costs
sections.summary: Elective egg freezing costs $7,000 to $9,000 per cycle in public hospitals and $10,000 to $15,000 in private clinics, with no subsidies, co-funding or Medisave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Elective egg freezing can cost between $7,000 and $9,000 per cycle in a public hospital, or $10,000 to $15,000 per cycle in a private fertility clinic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there are no subsidies, co-funding, or Medisave available for elective egg freezing.

sections.label: PSP calls for subsidies
sections.summary: PSP calls on the Government to consider subsidies in public hospitals and allow MediSave use for elective egg freezing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP therefore calls on the Government to consider some level of subsidies in public hospitals and allow the use of MediSave for this procedure.

sections.label: Co-funding after failed IVF
sections.summary: MOH is asked to consider allowing couples who failed two IVF cycles in a public hospital to receive co-funding at a private clinic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MOH consider allowing couples who have failed two IVF cycles in a public hospital to receive co-funding for treatment at a private clinic?

sections.label: Hospital ward waiting times
sections.summary: In December 2023, median waiting time to be warded was around 17 to 20 hours, exceeding 20 hours in certain hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In December 2023, the median waiting time to be warded was around 17 to 20 hours, and even exceeded 20 hours in certain hospitals.

sections.label: Smoking healthcare cost estimate
sections.summary: Healthcare costs and lost productivity caused by smoking in Singapore are estimated at at least $600 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The healthcare costs and lost productivity caused by smoking in Singapore has been estimated to be at least $600 million a year.

sections.label: Cohort smoking ban review
sections.summary: In January 2023 MOH said it is reviewing international practices on cohort smoking bans, and the UK plans to raise the minimum smoking age yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In January 2023, MOH stated that it is reviewing international practices on cohort smoking bans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The United Kingdom (UK) plans to increase the minimum smoking age every year until eventually no person can illegally buy cigarettes.

sections.label: Cohort smoking ban proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges a cohort smoking ban for those born on or after 2010, citing rising healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This forward-looking approach ensures that today's adults can make their own choices while laying the groundwork for a healthier legacy for their children and grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to implement a cohort smoking ban for all individuals in Singapore born on or after 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will give us four years to prepare new smoking regulations before we see our first smoke-free generation for all children aged 14 and under today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Healthcare costs have grown rapidly and the MOH budget is now second only to that of the Ministry of Defence.

sections.label: Capitation funding benchmarking studies
sections.summary: The question asks what benchmarking studies and targets exist to get healthcare systems and insurers to pursue cost savings under capitation funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With the move to capitation funding, what benchmarking studies have been done and what targets have been set to get healthcare systems and insurers to go after cost savings.

sections.label: Value-based healthcare pilot updates
sections.summary: The question asks for updates on pilot status, results, scaling up, and value-based healthcare's expected contribution to bending the cost curve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on the status of these pilots, what results have come out of them, whether some have been scaled up across the healthcare system and why or why not?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is the expected contribution of value-based healthcare to bending the cost curve.

sections.label: Digital technology and AI use
sections.summary: The question asks what MOH is doing to further harness the potential of digital technology and AI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is MOH doing to further harness the potential of digital technology and AI?

sections.label: Addressing transportation barriers
sections.summary: The passage states addressing transportation barriers could involve subsidies, medical transport services, telehealth, and supportive HDB and public transport designs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, addressing transportation barriers could involve subsidies for transportation costs for low income families and scaling up medical transport services, but they can also involve promoting telehealth services, as well as ensuring that HDB and public transportation designs are supportive of people with mobility needs.

sections.label: Supporting ageing caregivers
sections.summary: The passage lists government caregiver measures and asks how the Government can better support ageing caregivers, citing Japan's technology examples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government has announced many measures to better support caregivers, from higher caregiving grants to enhanced caregiving services and training, to pushing for flexible work arrangements to facilitating special needs trust services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Plans under Age Well SG, such as shared stay-in senior care services sandbox, are welcomed, but we must ensure that the solutions are scalable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, Japan has been at the forefront of leveraging technology, with robotic assistants, robotic exoskeletons, telepresence robots and smart home systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How can the Government better support ageing caregivers?

sections.label: Stay-in Shared Caregiving Sandbox details
sections.summary: MP asks MOH for details of the Stay-in Shared Caregiving Sandbox, single-point of contact plan, and scaling timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As such, I am delighted to hear that MOH, AIC and MOM have recently rolled out the Stay-in Shared Caregiving Sandbox, where five companies will come on board to serve an estimated 800 senior clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MOH share more about the details of this sandbox, such as the expected range and pricing of the services, whether the Government will be putting aside spaces within HDB estates to efficiently house these professional caregivers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MOH also share about the proposed single-point of contact plan which is part of Age Well SG and whether this single-point of contact plan will lead to better flow of information which can then be incorporated into this sandbox?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: It will also be helpful if MOH can provide an update on when they intend to scale up the sandbox to the rest of Singapore and whether constituencies like Kebun Baru with a congregation of seniors in both public and private estates can be considered for early inclusion into this subsequent roll-out or pilot.

sections.label: Community caregiver resource centres
sections.summary: MP recommends MOH work with MSF to set up community-based caregiver resource centres and train the community in caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Luckily, because I have been looking into caregiver provisions and interacting with residents who are caregivers, I found myself much more equipped to know what to do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I recommend that MOH work closely with MSF to set up community-based caregiver resource centres in every neighbourhood and start training the community with caregiving knowledge and navigation of resources before the care avalanche overwhelms a generation of Singaporeans.

sections.label: MOH smoking reduction strategies
sections.summary: MOH has implemented strategies to reduce smoking rates and prevent adoption of alternative smoking habits such as e-vaporisers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOH has been at the forefront of this battle, implementing comprehensive strategies to reduce smoking rates and preventing the adoption of alternative smoking habits, such as e-vaporisers.

sections.label: Anti-vaping and smoking plans
sections.summary: MP asks about MOH's ongoing plans and future strategies to minimise smoking rates, particularly anti-vaping measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's ongoing plans and future strategies to minimise smoking rates, particularly concerning anti-vaping measures?

sections.label: Culturally sensitive smoking interventions
sections.summary: MP asks what initiatives MOH has undertaken to decrease smoking prevalence and support ethnic groups in healthier lifestyles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This endeavour, however, cannot be successful without considering the cultural and socio-economic factors that influence lifestyle choices.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, what initiatives has MOH undertaken to decrease the smoking prevalence and to support the different ethnic groups in leading healthier lifestyles, including details on culturally sensitive interventions to address both physical health disparities and also acknowledge the potential role of mental well-being?

sections.label: Mental healthcare progress and strategies
sections.summary: MP asks what progress MOH has made in mental healthcare and its forthcoming strategies to enhance community accessibility and integration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To that end, I would like to ask: what progress has MOH made in advancing mental healthcare and what are the forthcoming strategies and structures being implemented to enhance the accessibility and integration of mental health services within the community?

sections.label: National Mental Health Office welcomed
sections.summary: Current service providers under MOH, MSF and MOE welcome the establishment of the National Mental Health Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Current service providers, whether under MOH, MSF or MOE, therefore, welcome the establishment of the National Mental Health Office.

sections.label: Age Well SG funding
sections.summary: The Government will dedicate at least S$3.5 billion over the next decade to Age Well SG, with S$1.9 billion for MOH initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To support these aspirations, the Government will dedicate at least S$3.5 billion over the next decade, to support the implementation of Age Well SG, of which S$1.9 billion will be dedicated to the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) initiatives.

sections.label: AAC centres expansion
sections.summary: AAC centres grew to 157, engaging over 49,000 seniors in 2022, and will expand to 220 by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since the implementation of the AAC service, we have grown to 157 AAC centres and have seen a steady increase in seniors engaged yearly – from 17,000 in 2021 to more than 49,000 seniors in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will do more and expand the network of AACs to 220 by the end of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This means that by 2025, eight in 10 seniors will have access to AAC activities near their homes.

sections.label: Silver Generation Office engagement
sections.summary: The Silver Generation Office and volunteer ambassadors engaged more than 330,000 seniors over the past four years through house visits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Together with volunteer ambassadors, the Silver Generation Office has engaged more than 330,000 seniors in the past fours years through house visits, including those who live alone or may have no family.

sections.label: MediSave schemes extended to homebound
sections.summary: Since October 2023, MediSave500/700 and Flexi-MediSave schemes have been extended to homebound patients receiving home medical care from MOH-funded providers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since October 2023, MediSave500/700 and Flexi-MediSave schemes have been extended to homebound patients receiving home medical care from MOH-funded providers.

sections.label: HPC+ pilot enrolment
sections.summary: As of January 2024, 328 clients are enrolled under the HPC+ pilot, which will be evaluated by end-2024.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: As of January 2024, there are 328 clients enrolled under the HPC+ pilot.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will evaluate the pilot by end-2024, before determining whether to expand it nationwide.

sections.label: Nursing home placement wait time
sections.summary: For seniors needing further care in Nursing Homes, the median wait time for nursing home placement is around one month.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For seniors who require further care in Nursing Homes, the median wait time for nursing home placement is around one month.

sections.label: Caregiver training subsidies
sections.summary: Since November 2023 caregivers can use SkillsFuture credits for eligible caregiver training, and the Caregivers Training Grant will be enhanced from $200 to up to $400 per year per care recipient.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since November 2023, caregivers have also been able to use their SkillsFuture credits for eligible caregiver training courses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This year, we will be enhancing the Caregivers Training Grant from the current $200 per year to up to $400 per year per care recipient, to subsidise the cost of caregiving training conducted by approved training providers.

sections.label: CAMH Strategy and Action Plan
sections.summary: The task force completed the CAMH Strategy and Action Plan, with 48 initiatives, of which 28 have been or are being implemented and the remainder are under review.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Relying on evidence-based research, such as the Growing Up in Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes, or GUSTO, study, we were able to formulate ways to improve the health of our children and families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am glad to announce that the task force has completed the development of the CAMH Strategy and Action Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Recommendations under the Strategy have been translated into 48 initiatives under the Action Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Currently, 28 out of the 48 initiatives have been or are being implemented, while the remainder are under review in preparation for launch.

sections.label: Antenatal education classes pilot
sections.summary: Antenatal education classes for parents will be piloted within the community to increase access to antenatal care.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Therefore, we have looked into increasing access to antenatal care.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that we will be piloting antenatal education classes for parents within the community.

sections.label: Infant and young child feeding guidelines
sections.summary: KK Women's and Children's Hospital and the College of Paediatrics and Child Health Singapore launched the Singapore Guidelines for Feeding and Eating in Infants and Young Children last month.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To better support individuals in nurturing healthy eating habits in children from young, I am happy to share that KK Women's and Children's Hospital and the College of Paediatrics and Child Health Singapore, launched the Singapore Guidelines for Feeding and Eating in Infants and Young Children last month.

sections.label: Summary of family health support
sections.summary: MOH has developed plans for strategies and action for the health and well-being of seniors, children and mothers, and will continue to strengthen support for families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Allow me to summarise in Malay. :   The MOH has developed plans for strategies and action for the health and well-being of seniors, as well as children and mothers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We have completed the development of CAMH, which focuses on various stages from prenatal to adolescence, developing initiatives to support children and families in areas, such as prenatal care, parental support and healthy eating habits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: These initiatives will empower and support our families in caring for our seniors and children. : In closing, families are fundamental to enabling our seniors to age well and to fostering a nurturing environment for our children to grow, learn and thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen support for families.

sections.label: Seniors driving hospital bed occupancy
sections.summary: Increased seniors with complex conditions post-COVID-19 raised average hospital stay from six to seven days, a 15% increase in patient load.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In Singapore, what is driving up hospital bed occupancy is the increased number of seniors with complex conditions post-COVID-19, and we saw a surge in the numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I have reported to the House earlier that average stay in hospital went up from about six days to seven days pre- and post-COVID-19, and that alone represents a 15% increase in patient load.

sections.label: Expanding hospital bed capacity
sections.summary: About 640 new acute and community hospital beds opened since June last year, with plans to add 4,000 beds by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To tackle the challenge more fundamentally, we need to expand capacity and catch up with the time lost, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We opened about 640 new acute and community hospital beds since June last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is the stock we have – 11,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We intend to add another 4,000 beds by 2030.

sections.label: New public hospital in Tengah
sections.summary: The next new public hospital should be in the West, planned for Tengah Town, an emerging population centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, the next new public hospital should be in the West.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are planning to site it in Tengah Town, which is an emerging population centre.

sections.label: Community hospital subsidy alignment
sections.summary: From the last quarter of this year, more diagnostic services and drugs will be subsidised at community hospitals, aligning subsidy frameworks at 50% to 80%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To remove this friction, from the last quarter of this year, we will allow more diagnostic services like CT and MRI scans and relevant drugs to be subsidised at community hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More broadly, we will also align the community hospital subsidy framework to the acute hospital subsidy framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That way, patients receive the same subsidy rate, which is 50% to 80% throughout their inpatient stay, regardless of settings.

sections.label: MIC@Home mainstream care model
sections.summary: From April this year, MIC@Home becomes a mainstream care model, with patients paying no more than for acute inpatient care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Having done this for several months, we are convinced that the scheme works well for the patients and has great potential to relieve stress at hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, from April this year, MIC@Home will become a mainstream model of care in our public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a result, patients can be assured that they will not pay any more for MIC@Home than they do for acute inpatient care in a public hospital.

sections.label: Expanding MIC@Home capacity
sections.summary: MIC@Home capacity will expand from 100 in 2023 to 300 in 2024, with potential to scale up further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will be better to develop MIC@Home into a well-accepted mainstream mode for acute inpatient care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will also further expand the capacity of MIC@Home, as a first step, from 100 in 2023, to 300 in 2024, with the potential to scale up further.

sections.label: Shortages in broad-based specialist areas
sections.summary: MOH is increasing training positions in family, internal, geriatric and rehabilitation medicine because Singapore's ageing society needs doctors with broad-based skillsets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: On the other hand, we are facing shortages in areas like family medicine, internal medicine, geriatric medicine and rehabilitation medicine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is because as Singapore becomes a super-aged society, we have more patients with complex and multiple medical conditions, needing doctors with these more broad-based skillsets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, MOH has been increasing the number of training positions in these specialist areas.

sections.label: Healthy life expectancy and healthcare spending
sections.summary: Singaporeans live to 74 years in good health, among the world's highest, while Singapore spends about 5% of GDP on healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In Singapore, a person is expected to live up to 74 years old in good health, one of the highest in the world; compared to 66 in the US; 70 in the UK; 71 to 72 in Germany, France, Denmark, Netherlands, Australia and so forth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Singapore achieved this by spending about 5% of our gross domestic product (GDP) on healthcare, compared to 10% to 13% in most developed countries; 17% in the US.

sections.label: Singapore's S+3Ms healthcare payment system
sections.summary: Singapore pays for healthcare through taxation-funded subsidies, MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund, called S+3Ms, so the uninsured are not underserved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But if someone did not buy insurance and is uninsured, they will be underserved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is why in Singapore, we weaved together a more robust way to pay for healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It comprises subsidy funded by taxation; MediSave which is own personal savings; MediShield Life which is a national insurance scheme; and MediFund which is the final social safety net – what we termed S+3Ms.

sections.label: MediFund for lowest income
sections.summary: MediFund helps the lowest income who cannot afford co-payment, a key reason for good outcomes at 5% of GDP spending.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MediFund comes in for the lowest income who cannot afford the co-payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is a key reason why we can achieve good health outcomes with national healthcare spending of 5% of GDP, compared to jurisdictions with blanket assistance schemes.

sections.label: MOH budget compared with ministries
sections.summary: MOH's budget has surpassed MOE's, reaching almost S$19 billion and not far behind MINDEF's.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOH's budget has far surpassed MOE's, to almost S$19 billion and not very far behind MINDEF's.

sections.label: Review of MediShield Life
sections.summary: A comprehensive review of MediShield Life will be conducted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To this end, we will be conducting a comprehensive review of MediShield Life.

sections.label: Hospital bill growth and MediShield Life
sections.summary: Public hospital bills grew 5% yearly and private 7%, so MediShield Life covers about eight in 10 subsidised bills, expected to slip further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Bill sizes have grown by 5% annually in public hospitals and by 7% annually in private hospitals over the last few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a result, the proportion of subsidised bills adequately covered by MediShield Life has come down to around eight out of 10 and is expected to slip further.

sections.label: Angioplasty claim limits example
sections.summary: For an angioplasty with a stent and a few nights in ICU, claim limits may need to double, times two.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For example, for an episode involving angioplasty where a stent is placed into your heart to open up a blocked artery, plus, say, a few nights in ICU, the claim limits may need to double, times two.

sections.label: Approved cancer drug prices
sections.summary: Prices for approved cancer drugs have since dropped significantly, some by up to 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a result, prices for approved cancer drugs have since dropped significantly, some by up to 60%.

sections.label: Premium increase at last review
sections.summary: At the last review of the scheme, premiums went up by 25% on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The last time we reviewed the scheme, premiums went up by 25% on average.

sections.label: Enrolment in family doctor programme
sections.summary: Since the programme launched in July last year, 2.4 million Singapore residents aged 40 and above were invited, and 765,000 enrolled as of last month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since the programme was launched in July last year, we have invited 2.4 million Singapore residents, aged 40 and above, to participate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of last month, 765,000 have enrolled with a family doctor of their choice.

sections.label: Free vaccinations and health screenings
sections.summary: More than 124,000 enrollees have received their free vaccinations and health screenings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More than 124,000 enrollees have received their free vaccinations and health screenings.

sections.label: Expanding care protocols
sections.summary: MOH will expand protocols to cover more conditions, including stable ischemic heart diseases and stable stroke.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOH will expand the range of protocols to cover more conditions, such as stable ischemic heart diseases and stable stroke.

sections.label: Lower-sodium salt supply
sections.summary: With much effort from HPB, over 60% of salt wholesalers now supply lower-sodium salt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With much effort from the HPB, over 60% of wholesalers of salt are now supplying lower-sodium salt.

sections.label: Services-centric healthcare regulation
sections.summary: Regulation moves from premises-centric to services-centric, so services are regulated regardless of setting, via the new Healthcare Services Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Regulation needs to move from being premises centric to services centric.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we do not regulate hospitals or clinics, but the services delivered, regardless of settings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is why we revamped our legislation to enact the new Healthcare Services Act (HCSA).

sections.label: Premises-neutrality rule changes
sections.summary: Situations for premises-neutrality are progressively identified and deliberate rule changes made, including MediFund recognition, MediSave for telehealth, community hospitals and MIC@Home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Instead, we progressively identify the situations and circumstances where premises-neutrality should apply, and then make deliberate rule changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We made a few changes last year on the mutual recognition of MediFund and extension of MediSave support to manage chronic illnesses via telehealth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This year, I just announced further moves on community hospitals, MIC@Home and MediSave support for telehealth.

sections.label: Singapore ranked best healthcare system
sections.summary: Rankings evaluate population health and preventive care systems, not just doctor ratios, capacity or equipment, and ranked Singapore best in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They do not just take into account of your doctor to population ratio or your healthcare capacity, or what kind of state of the art equipment you use, but they also evaluate population health and preventive care systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They ranked Singapore as having the best healthcare system in the world in 2023.

sections.label: More polyclinics for ageing population
sections.summary: There are 25 polyclinics and over 1,000 Healthier SG GP clinics today; by 2030 there will be 32 polyclinics, with three new ones in the western region.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about plans to build more polyclinics to cater to the increasing demands of our ageing population, particularly in the Western region.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: There are 25 polyclinics and over 1,000 Healthier SG GP clinics today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: By 2030, we will have 32 polyclinics and we hope to have more Healthier SG GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: There will be three new polyclinics in the western region: one in Tengah which will be completed by 2025, another in Yew Tee by 2027 and the third in Taman Jurong by 2028.

sections.label: Office establishment by 2025
sections.summary: The Office is expected to be fully established by 2025 with officers from MOH, MSF and MOE.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Office is expected to be fully established by 2025, comprising officers from MOH, MSF and MOE.

sections.label: Mental health in polyclinics
sections.summary: 19 of 25 polyclinics provide mental health services, and support will expand to all polyclinics and Healthier SG clinics by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Today, 19 out of the existing 25 polyclinics provide mental health services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To bring mental health services closer to where individuals live, we will expand mental health support in all polyclinics and Healthier SG clinics by 2030.

sections.label: Outreach and COMIT teams
sections.summary: Outreach teams will expand to 90 by 2030, and Community Intervention Teams from 29 to 50 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: By 2030, we will expand the number of outreach teams to 90.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For those who require more intensive mental health support, they can be referred to any of our 29 Community Intervention Teams (COMIT), which will be expanded to 50 teams by 2030.

sections.label: Healthier SG care protocols
sections.summary: Twelve care protocols were released at the Healthier SG launch on common chronic conditions and preventive health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Twelve care protocols were released during the launch of Healthier SG on the management of common chronic conditions, such as diabetes, high cholesterol and preventive health, such as smoking cessation and weight management.

sections.label: PCN clinic participation growth
sections.summary: Clinics participating in a PCN grew from 340 in 2018 to more than 1,000 today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The number of clinics participating in a PCN has grown, from 340 clinics in 2018, to more than 1,000 clinics today.

sections.label: National Electronic Health Record tool
sections.summary: The National Electronic Health Record is a key tool for supporting holistic and integrated care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) is a key tool for supporting holistic and integrated care.

sections.label: Health Information Bill framework
sections.summary: The Health Information Bill will establish a framework governing collection, access, use and sharing of selected health information across settings to facilitate continuity of care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The upcoming Health Information Bill will also establish the framework to govern the collection, access, use and sharing of selected health information across various settings to facilitate the continuity of care.

sections.label: Cancer Drug List outcomes
sections.summary: Since the Cancer Drug List was implemented, public sector CDL drug prices fell by an average of 30%, allowing more subsidies and improved affordability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Since the implementation of the Cancer Drug List (CDL), which focused MediShield Life and Integrated Shield Plan coverage on clinically proven and cost-effective cancer drug treatments, CDL drug prices in the public sector have been brought down by an average of 30%, and over 60% for some drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This has also allowed us to subsidise more drugs and improve affordability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In the long run, we expect this to moderate the costs of cancer drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are shifting our focus more upstream and are applying value-based care to payment models, like capitation and preventive efforts through Healthier SG.

sections.label: Consistent primary care and health plans
sections.summary: Consistent, evidence-based care will be delivered across the diverse primary care landscape, and everyone can take proactive steps to keep to a personalised health plan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Consistent and evidence-based care will be delivered across the diverse primary care landscape, and all of us can take proactive steps to keep to a personalised health plan.

sections.label: Healthcare manpower and student intake growth
sections.summary: Over 10 years, healthcare manpower grew about 40% and local healthcare student intakes rose similarly, giving a combined intake of 3,600 students in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, we grew our healthcare manpower by about 40% and increased our local healthcare student intakes at our IHLs by a similar margin, translating to a combined intake of 3,600 healthcare students in 2023.

sections.label: ANGEL scheme for nurses
sections.summary: The Award for Nurses' Grace, Excellence and Loyalty (ANGEL) scheme was announced last month for nurses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For nurses, we announced the Award for Nurses' Grace, Excellence and Loyalty (ANGEL) scheme last month.

sections.label: Starting salary increases 2023
sections.summary: Starting salaries for nurses, allied health professionals and pharmacists were increased by up to 12% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, starting salaries for nurses, allied health professionals and pharmacists were increased by up to 12% in 2023.

sections.label: Nurse recruitment target exceeded
sections.summary: In 2023, Singapore exceeded its national target of bringing 4,000 new nurses into the workforce, so the situation on the ground is expected to improve.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2023, we also exceeded our national target of bringing 4,000 new nurses into our workforce and, with that, we can expect the situation on the ground to improve.

sections.label: Obesity prevalence rising
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey 2022 showed obesity prevalence rose from 8.6% in 2013 to 10.5% in 2020 and 11.6% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The National Population Health Survey 2022 also showed that the prevalence of obesity has continued to increase, from 8.6% in 2013, to 10.5% in 2020, and 11.6% in 2022.

sections.label: Tobacco control measures and smoking prevalence
sections.summary: Standardised packaging, raising the minimum legal smoking age to 21 and a 15% tobacco tax rise, with Healthier SG cessation support, helped achieve an all-time low smoking prevalence of 9.2% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Our recent efforts include the Standardised Packaging measures, raising the Minimum Legal Age of smoking to 21 years old and raising tobacco taxes by 15% last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Cessation support is also strengthened through Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These efforts have continued to suppress smoking prevalence and we have achieved an all-time low of 9.2% in 2022.

sections.label: HPB quit journey support
sections.summary: In 2023, HPB supported 4,700 adults and 2,300 children and youths in their quit journey.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2023, HPB supported 4,700 adults and 2,300 children and youths in their quit journey.

sections.label: Vaping penalties and ethnic minority health programmes
sections.summary: Legal penalties for vaping will be reviewed for deterrence, and over 40,000 Malay/Muslim and over 32,000 Indian residents joined healthy living programmes in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Even while we step up enforcement and education efforts, we will be reviewing the legal penalties to ensure a strong deterrence against vaping and related offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To Dr Wan Rizal's question, we have kept up the momentum of our efforts to support ethnic minority groups to lead healthier lifestyles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I am encouraged to share that with the strong support from community leaders and organisations, over 40,000 Malay/Muslim residents and over 32,000 Indian residents participated in healthy living programmes encompassing physical activities, health talks and Saham Kesihatan programmes, as well as healthier groceries distribution during the festive periods of Ramadan, Hari Raya and Deepavali, in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Health Task Force will strengthen efforts to encourage Healthier SG enrolment among the Indian community to supplement HPB's existing collaborations with the Hindu Endowment Board, Sikh Welfare Association, among other partners.

sections.label: Lose To Win weight loss
sections.summary: Her desire to motivate others to adopt a healthier lifestyle stemmed from her own transformation through HPB's Lose To Win programme, where she shed about 16 kilogrammes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Her fervent desire to motivate others to adopt a healthier lifestyle stemmed from her own transformation through HPB's Lose To Win programme, where she managed to shed about 16 kilogrammes.

sections.label: Means-testing for long-term care subsidies
sections.summary: Long-term care subsidies are means-tested using per capita household income and residence Annual Value, and the Government recently raised these thresholds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: First, at the earlier Budget debate, Ms Jessica Tan requested clarifications on our means-testing criteria for long-term care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These subsidies are means-tested using per capita household income (PCHI) and Annual Value (AV) of residence to ensure that subsidies are targeted at those who need it more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To ensure that those with greater needs receive continued support, the Government recently raised the PCHI and AV thresholds for all means-tested social support schemes and grants.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant and SMA treatments
sections.summary: Home Caregiving Grant payouts rose in 2023 to up to $400 monthly, and treatments for spinal muscular atrophy are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, in 2023, the payouts under the Home Caregiving Grant were increased, from $200, to up to $400 per month to further reduce caregiving costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Fourth, to Mr Ong Hua Han's question on the support for patients with spinal muscular atrophy, there are a few treatments available currently, including drugs and a CTGTP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are reviewing the clinical and cost-effectiveness of these treatments and are engaging pharmaceutical companies to achieve reasonable prices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As the Minister mentioned, the MediShield Life Council is considering extending coverage to eligible CTGTPs and studying the safeguards needed to ensure that any such extension is sustainable.

sections.label: Fertility test subsidies at public clinics
sections.summary: At public specialist outpatient clinics, couples can enjoy subsidies of up to 70% for their fertility tests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: At our public specialist outpatient clinics, these couples can enjoy subsidies of up to 70% for their fertility tests.

sections.label: IVF co-funding at public centres
sections.summary: Co-funding applies to in vitro fertilisation at public assisted reproduction centres, which have sufficient capacity with utilisation rates of about 61%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Co-funding also applies to those who are undergoing in vitro fertilisation (IVF) at public assisted reproduction centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These public centres currently have sufficient capacity, with utilisation rates of about 61%.

sections.label: Reviewing co-funding at private centres
sections.summary: Some couples may prefer private centres, and it is being reviewed whether to extend co-funding to these settings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we recognise that some couples may prefer seeking treatment at private centres and are reviewing whether to extend co-funding to these settings.

sections.label: Non-emergency A&E cases
sections.summary: Emergencies can be defined differently by patients and medical professionals, and about 40% of A&E cases are not emergency cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Emergencies can be defined by the patient and the medical professional differently depending on the sort of pain you are in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And to that end, the Minister shared that about 40% of cases at Accidents and Emergencies (A&Es) are not emergency cases.

sections.label: Overstayers numbers in Singapore
sections.summary: Overstayers fell from about 300 to 200 at any point in time, with room for improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On overstayers, actually I have addressed that question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We used to have about 300 overstayers at any point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It has come down to 200, but there is still room for improvement.

sections.label: Singapore private healthcare insurance premium
sections.summary: Singapore's current private healthcare insurance premium is the third highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our current private healthcare insurance premium now in Singapore is the third highest in the world.

sections.label: Private insurance premium increase
sections.summary: Private insurance premium has risen about 20% per year, a rate the speaker calls unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Private insurance premium has gone up by about 20% per year and this is not a sustainable rate in my opinion.

sections.label: Public health institutions day surgery
sections.summary: Public health institutions have tried to convert as many surgeries as possible to day or outpatient surgery, and length of stay increased pre- and post-pandemic to six to seven days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Our public health institutions have been trying to convert as many surgeries as possible to day surgery and, like the Member mentioned, outpatient surgery if possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I mentioned length of stay increased pre- and post-pandemic, six to seven days.

sections.label: Workload increase
sections.summary: That is a 15% increase in workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Even that, as I mentioned, is a 15% increase in workload.

sections.label: Raising MediShield Life claim limits
sections.summary: Because hospital bills for significant episodes are growing, raising MediShield Life claim limits for subsidised patients with major healthcare episodes is needed to control healthcare costs for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It has an impact mostly because hospital bills, especially for significant episodes, are getting larger and increasing year by year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Therefore, if we want to control healthcare costs for the families, we need to raise claims limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Increase the claim limits of MediShield Life, which means it is for subsidised patients when they have a major healthcare episode.

sections.label: Insurance companies competing on unsustainable terms
sections.summary: The speaker is not aware but will take a look, noting insurance companies compete for market share with unsustainable terms despite rising premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I am not aware, but we can take a look.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But I do have to say, as I mentioned, with some frustration in my speech just now, despite rising premiums, I still see insurance companies competing for market share, offering terms that are obviously unsustainable.

sections.label: Directly appointing local providers
sections.summary: The speaker says they will consider directly appointing providers who already have an established local presence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To the Member's query, yes, we will consider directly appointing providers who already have an established local presence.

sections.label: MediShield Life review and Healthier SG
sections.summary: The speaker warns against being too ambitious and says it is too early to consider Healthier SG's blunting effect in the MediShield Life review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Do not be too ambitious and jump to a level that you cannot cope, where doctors and nurses cannot cope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for MediShield Life review, how to take into account the blunting effect of Healthier SG, I think it is too early.

sections.label: MediSave and MediShield Life claim limits
sections.summary: As MediShield Life claim limits go up, MediSave coverage of the remainder will be correspondingly reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As claim limits goes up for MediShield Life, whatever that is remaining, you want to make sure that MediSave can also cover them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, there will be a corresponding review as we increase MediShield Life limits.

sections.label: Effectiveness of elective egg freezing
sections.summary: The speaker states the effectiveness of elective egg freezing is not really something that has been proven.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The effectiveness of elective egg freezing is not really something that has been proven.

sections.label: MIC@Home and caregiver training grants
sections.summary: The speaker calls MIC@Home progressive and promising, and welcomes enhancements to caregiver training grants and SkillsFuture credits for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I think the MIC@Home seems to be very progressive and very promising.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also glad that Second Minister Masagos announced that there will be enhancements to the caregiver training grants, as well as the SkillsFuture credits for caregivers who receive training.

sections.label: Mainstreaming MIC@Home and caregiver support
sections.summary: Mainstreaming MIC@Home is approached clinically, while caregiver support including finances, respite care and training needs review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: When we decide to mainstream MIC@Home, we are really approaching it from a clinical angle, which is, we think we are confident enough – by our hospitals – to set up the right equipment, train the caregivers and able to support the patient to recover at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But I think Ms Carrie Tan is coming from a different perspective, which is about home care grant and how to support a caregiver who may have to give up their employment and their job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think it is something we have to review to see how best we can support caregivers, not just financially, but also in terms of their caregiving duties; giving them respite care services; proper training.

sections.label: Sembawang MIC@Home helped hospital ED
sections.summary: The first MIC@Home started in Sembawang GRC and helped Khoo Teck Puat Hospital's ED manage its load.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In fact, the first one that started was in Sembawang Group Representation Constituency (GRC) and over the years, it greatly helped Khoo Teck Puat Hospital's ED, helped them manage their ED load and it has proven to be useful.

sections.label: Doctor-to-population ratio increasing
sections.summary: The doctor-to-population ratio has been increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As to our own doctor-to-population ratio, it has been increasing.

sections.label: Places taken up doubled
sections.summary: 100,000 places were taken up in FY2020 and this doubled in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, 100,000 places were taken up in FY2020 and it has doubled in 2023.

sections.label: Nursing home waiting time and AIC Link
sections.summary: While waiting for nursing home placement, medically stable public hospital patients can make longer-term arrangements, with AIC Link in every hospital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On the waiting time for nursing home, while waiting for placement at nursing home, there are ways which we can help our patients – particularly those, for example, who are medically stable in our public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: There, they can work out the longer-term arrangements while waiting for a nursing home to be available if they are not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: There is one touchpoint in every hospital, which is the AIC Link.

sections.label: COMIT, CREST and pricing gradient
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State will comment on COMIT and CREST, and pricing at a gradient gives patients a strong signal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I will ask Senior Minister of State to comment on COMIT and CREST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think even as a policy of pricing, you want to price it at a gradient so that patients get a strong signal.

sections.label: Support for community care practitioners
sections.summary: The speaker agrees primary and community care practitioners need adequate support and says teams are being increased because the planned increase is not yet achieved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I agree with the sentiment that we need to make sure that our primary care practitioners and the whole community of community care practitioners is adequately supported.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have not yet achieved the increase that we are planning for, so we are increasing the teams.
